title: fix(plugin-auth): the invitation role cap's refusals carry their error codes, and a membership read fault answers 503
body:
Fixes #23945

Clause-②: no

## What changes

The invitation role cap in `beforeCreateInvitation` refused with `403` and a message, but no `code`. better-auth's own `owner` refusal on the same endpoint (`POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member`) carries one. Each of the cap's three refusals now carries the code #24082 registered for it under `@objectstack/plugin-auth`. A membership read that throws now answers as a store outage, not as a refusal.

| the cap's branch (`invitation-role-cap.ts`) | status | body `code` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the requested role grades above the issuer's own | 403 | `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER` |
| an issuer below admin grade asked for a role other than `member` | 403 | `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` |
| the issuer's role was not established (an answered read with no usable row, or no data engine) | 403 | `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` |
| the issuer's `sys_member` read **threw** (was 403 with no code, through the branch above) | **503** | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |

- `invitationRoleCapFailure()` returns `{ code, message }` from each branch instead of a bare string. The three codes are exported constants typed `RegisteredErrorCode`, so a removed or misspelled ledger row fails `tsc` (reverse-verified below). The verdicts do not change: the same invitations are admitted and refused.
- The hook throws `new APIError('FORBIDDEN', { message, code })`, the body shape `remove-member` and the vendor's `owner` refusal already use. better-call passes `body` through verbatim, so `code` reaches the wire (measured below).
- `resolveMembershipRole` used to end in `catch { return null; }`, which turned a thrown read into the unverified verdict. It now throws `invitationRoleCapReadFaultApiError(err)`: `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, the driver's error on `cause`. This is the slug guard's shape (`slugGuardReadFaultApiError`), with one difference: this body carries `code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` too, so every answer from this endpoint has a code. Still fail-closed: the throw ends the endpoint, so no invitation row is written.
- The ledger comment on `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` is reworded to what the emitter does now. The phrase "or the lookup did not answer" is gone. The comment now covers the no-engine exit and names the 503 for a read that throws. The three-line block comment above it said "today the cap throws a bare `FORBIDDEN`". That is false after this PR, so it is reworded too (see Deviations). Both are comment-only, and no code is added, removed or renamed.

## The seat's rulings on #24082's four review points (premise measured first)

1. **Split the outage from the refusal.** Premise holds. The cap's read path could not tell a thrown read from an empty answer, and the place that merged them is the cap's own read: `resolveMembershipRole`'s `catch { return null; }` (`auth-manager.ts`, the last line of the method on `6e43b7bc3f`). Its one caller is `beforeCreateInvitation` (`git grep resolveMembershipRole` finds the definition and one call). The split is made at that read.
2. **The no-engine exit fails closed.** It already returned `null`, which grades below a plain member, so it answers `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` (403). This PR keeps it that way and pins it. Reachability: no shipped composition reaches the hook without an engine. `AuthPlugin` hard-depends on ObjectQL (`dependencies`, `requiresServices: ['data', …]`), and `ctx.getService('data')` throws when the service is absent. The one production construction, `auth-plugin.ts` `new AuthManager(authConfig)`, always passes `dataEngine`. A bare `AuthManager` built without `dataEngine` (an exported class, documented as usable outside the plugin) runs better-auth on its in-memory adapter and does reach the hook with nothing to read. The ledger comment covers that exit.
3. **Is the "no row" input (`:175`) reachable through the public door?** Measured on the wire, once, with a throwaway dogfood probe that was deleted afterwards (showcase boot at `313560aef`):
   - a user with a live session and no membership row, inviting as `admin`: **400** `{"message":"Member not found","code":"MEMBER_NOT_FOUND"}`. better-auth's own refusal, so the hook never ran. (The first try answered 401: ending a membership ends its sessions, so the probe signs in again first.)
   - a plain `member`, inviting as `admin`: **403** `{"message":"You are not allowed to invite users to this organization","code":"YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_INVITE_USERS_TO_THIS_ORGANIZATION"}`. Again before the hook.
   - The installed better-auth 1.7.3 source agrees (`plugins/organization/routes/crud-invites.mjs`). `findMemberByOrgId`, then `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, then `hasPermission(invitation:create)`, all run before `beforeCreateInvitation`. The cap then re-reads the same `sys_member` rows in system context.
   - So `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` has no input that reaches it through this door. Getting there needs the row to vanish between the two reads. It is pinned at the unit level (`auth-manager.test.ts`, "an unresolvable issuer membership fails CLOSED", which says why in a comment). The two reachable codes are pinned on the wire in the dogfood file.
4. **All three codes get their emitter here.** Each refusal carries its `code` through better-auth's `APIError` body. `check:error-code-provenance` sees the three constant definitions as stamp sites listed under `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (exit 0, "every registered-code stamp site is listed under its own owner key").

## PM mechanism hypotheses

- `auth-manager.ts` threw `new APIError('FORBIDDEN', { message: capFailure })`, and `invitationRoleCapFailure()` returned a bare string from three branches. **Holds** on `6e43b7bc3f`.
- better-auth serialises `APIError`'s `code` into the body. **Holds, and a custom code travels the same way.** better-call 1.4.0 `InternalAPIError` stores `body` verbatim. `APIError.from` (the vendor's `owner` refusal) only builds `{ message, code }` from its error record. Measured on the wire: `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER` and `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` arrive as `body.code` (dogfood, below).
- `delegated-admin-invite.dogfood.test.ts` already drives these refusals. **Holds** for `admin`. It had no `delegated_admin`-by-delegate case, so one is added.

## Clause-② measured

`no`. On the built entry declarations: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/dist/index.d.ts` and `index.d.mts` carry 0 occurrences of `invitationRoleCapFailure`, `InvitationRoleCapRefusal` and the three `*_CODE` constants. The control `class AuthManager` appears 1 time, and `rate-limit-storage.d.ts` has 0. `invitation-role-cap.ts` is not re-exported from `src/index.ts`. The only declaration text that moved is the doc comment on the private `resolveMembershipRole`. For `@objectstack/spec`, `check:api-surface` answered "public API surface + factory signatures unchanged". The ledger edit is a comment, so `ErrorCode` accepts the same strings. Nothing widens an accept-set: no invitation is newly admitted, and no code is added.

## Tests (at `313560aef`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (the whole package): `Test Files 158 passed (158)`, `Tests 3096 passed | 10 skipped (3106)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0. It includes `check:test-typecheck`: "test layer compiles … 10 file(s) / 88 error(s) / 23 pinned signature(s) held".
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts src/api/api-error-code-type.test.ts`: `Tests 24 passed (24)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` lists the edited dogfood file once.
- Dogfood on the wire, after building `@objectstack/dogfood^...` (66 tasks): `test/delegated-admin-invite.dogfood.test.ts`, `Tests 5 passed`, including "the same delegate issuing `admin` is REFUSED" (`body.code` `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER`) and the new "the same delegate minting another delegate is REFUSED as member-only" (`body.code` `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY`, no `sys_invitation` row).
- ESLint `--no-inline-config` over the seven changed `.ts` files: exit 0.

Refusal tests assert the envelope (`statusCode`, `status`, `body.code`), not a bare throw. The cap's unit tests now assert codes rather than prose. The parity oracle in `invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts` spells the codes as literals, so its grid of over 100 refusals also pins which branch answers which code.

**Ablation** (one-time, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`). The unit tests import `./auth-manager` from source, so no `dist/` rebuild applies:
- A: drop `code: refusal.code` from the throw. The run went red with `Tests 5 failed | 3 passed`: the `admin`, member-only, unresolvable, no-engine and before-placement cases. The two admit cases and the 503 case stayed green. Restored, blob `698973c2e6c6` equal to HEAD.
- B: replace the read fault's `throw` with `return null` (the old swallow). The run went red with `Tests 1 failed | 7 passed`: the 503 case failed with "expected 403 to be 503". Restored, blob equal to HEAD.

**Reverse verification** of the `RegisteredErrorCode` annotation: misspelling the first constant as `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER_TYPO` turns `tsc --noEmit` red with `TS2820 … Did you mean '"INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER"'?`. Restored.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on this diff derives the same 91 commands as the seat's list. All 91 were run locally at `313560aef`, each exit captured before any pipe. 90 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it needs a whole-workspace build), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI's `Build Core`. `--ran`: "✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 91 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 90 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)." The PR's check-runs had not reported when this was written.

## Acceptance notes

- **The organization slug guard's 503 body carries no `code`** (`slugGuardReadFaultApiError`). That is the same gap this PR addresses for the cap's read fault, on `update-organization`. It is reachable only through a store fault, and no public door produces one on demand, so it is noted here and not filed. Carrier: none.
- **`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts`** still describes the cap's refusals as "a bare `FORBIDDEN` today" and names the case "registered ahead of their plugin-auth producer". That is history once this lands. It is not on this PR's surface, so it is left alone. Carrier: none.
- **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json`** `identity-auth.invitation-scope-gates` scores the admin-role refusal as "non-2xx". It could now name `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER`. Carrier: none.

## Deviations

- The ledger's three-line block comment above the rows is reworded as well as the `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` comment. It said "today the cap throws a bare `FORBIDDEN`, and #23945 stamps these", which this PR makes false. Comment-only, same file, same rows.
- `origin/main` moved 6 commits after the branch point (`6e43b7bc3` to `7715d049e`). None touches a file in this diff. It is not merged in: this PR's CI runs on the merge ref, and the queue re-verifies on its rebuilt generation.
